chapters.1.lds: Why does Micah mourn while announcing judgment?
chapters.1.summary: The LORD’s word comes to Micah of Moresheth about Samaria and Jerusalem. The LORD comes down, and the mountains melt under him. Samaria will become a heap of rubble. Its idols will be smashed. Micah says he will wail and go barefoot and naked. The wound has reached the gate of Jerusalem. He names town after town in Judah’s lowlands. Each one will share in the disaster and the exile.
chapters.2.lds: Who loses shelter when powerful people seize inherited fields?
chapters.2.summary: Micah speaks against those who plan evil on their beds. At dawn they carry it out, since it is in their power. They covet fields and houses and seize them. They rob a man of his home and his inheritance. So God is planning disaster against them. They tell Micah not to preach such things. They drive women from their homes and take the children’s blessing. Yet God will gather the remnant like sheep.
chapters.3.lds: How does payment change the messages people receive?
chapters.3.summary: Micah addresses the rulers of Israel, who should know justice. They hate good and treat the people like meat for the pot. Prophets promise peace to those who feed them. They declare war on those who give them nothing. Micah says he is filled with the LORD’s Spirit to declare Israel’s sin. Leaders judge for bribes, priests teach for pay, and prophets speak for money. They say the LORD is among them. So Zion will be plowed like a field.
chapters.4.lds: In 3 Nephi 20:18–19 Jesus repeats the sheaves and iron horn. Who receives a place in the promised gathering?
chapters.4.summary: In later days the mountain of the LORD’s house will be raised above the hills. Nations will come to learn his ways. He will judge between peoples and settle their disputes. They will beat swords into plows and learn war no more. Everyone will sit under his own vine and fig tree, unafraid. God will gather the lame and those who were driven away. He will rule them on Mount Zion. For now Zion must go to Babylon, and there she will be rescued.
chapters.5.lds: The lesson’s children’s section connects Bethlehem with Jesus through Matthew’s account of his birth. How does feeding a flock change the image of a threatened ruler?
chapters.5.summary: Jerusalem is under siege, and its ruler is struck on the cheek. A new ruler will come from Bethlehem, a small town in Judah. His origins are from ancient times. He will stand and shepherd his flock in the LORD’s strength. His people will live securely. He will be their peace when Assyria invades. The remnant of Jacob will be like dew among the nations. God will remove their horses, forts, and idols.
chapters.6.lds: The lesson asks readers to consider the conduct Micah says God requires. How do false weights contradict the conduct God requires?
chapters.6.summary: The LORD brings a case against his people, with the mountains as witnesses. He asks what he has done to weary them. He brought them from Egypt and sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. A worshiper asks what he should bring to the LORD. He offers calves, thousands of rams, and even his firstborn. The answer is that God has already shown what is good. Do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with God. The city, however, is full of false weights and violence.
chapters.7.lds: The lesson’s introduction emphasizes God’s delight in mercy through Micah’s final praise. Why does the ending join admitted wrongdoing with hope for forgiveness?
chapters.7.summary: Micah grieves like someone who finds no fruit after the harvest. The faithful have vanished, and officials take bribes. No one can trust a neighbor or even a family member. Yet Micah will watch and wait for the LORD. He admits his sin and expects God to plead his case. He asks God to shepherd his people. He asks who is a God like this, who pardons guilt. God will hurl all their sins into the depths of the sea.
